finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.sink: Reading the password from the 'secret' file
finding.trigger: If the 'secret' file contains malicious content, it could be executed as a command
finding.assumptions: The 'secret' file is expected to contain only the password, but if it contains any command or script, it could be executed

parsed.refutation_attempt: No path from the 'secret' file contents to any OS command execution. The password string is only passed to libcurl via CURLOPT_PASSWORD (line 54). There is no system, exec, or similar call that interprets the password as a command.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.untrusted_source: The password read from the 'secret' file
finding.sink: Using the password in the SMTP authentication
finding.trigger: If the password contains any command or script, it could be executed
finding.assumptions: The password is expected to be plain text, but if it contains any command or script, it could be executed

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code passes the password string directly to libcurl's CURLOPT_PASSWORD option, which is used only for SMTP authentication. libcurl does not interpret this value as a shell command; it simply transmits it over the network to the SMTP server. Therefore, there is no path from the file‑read source to an OS command execution sink. The relevant lines are 32-38 for reading the file, 54 for setting the option, and 70-72 for performing the request. No check or sanitization is required because the operation is not a command execution.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.sink: Using the email sender address in the SMTP authentication
finding.trigger: If the email sender address contains any command or script, it could be executed
finding.assumptions: The email sender address is expected to be plain text, but if it contains any command or script, it could be executed

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked source of mail_from: it is a hard‑coded constant defined at line 41. Since it is not derived from any user‑controllable input (stdin, file, network, argv, environment, IPC, or API parameter), it does not satisfy the first condition for a vulnerability. The sink is a libcurl option (CURLOPT_MAIL_FROM) which only sets an SMTP header; it does not invoke a shell or system command, so no command injection is possible. No path exists from an untrusted source to a dangerous operation.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.sink: Using the email recipient address in the SMTP authentication
finding.trigger: If the email recipient address contains any command or script, it could be executed
finding.assumptions: The email recipient address is expected to be plain text, but if it contains any command or script, it could be executed

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the source of the data used in the recipient list. The address "spam.mhered@gmail.com" is a compile‑time constant defined on line 42, not derived from any external input such as stdin, file, network, argv, environment, or IPC. Since the data is not untrusted, no path exists from an attacker‑controlled source to the sink on line 58. The sink itself merely passes the address to libcurl's internal data structure; libcurl does not invoke a shell or system command with this value. Thus the OS command injection claim is unfounded.
